newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and PIBOR futures ended the day higher despite much stronger than expected U.S. economic data which sent U.S. markets reeling.

The franc rallied strongly on the day, supported by a much better than expected French unemployment report which showed that the number of people unemployed in France dropped by a seasonally-adjusted 20,000 in July.

The report was seen as a shaft of sunlight in an otherwise gloomy economic landscape and was expected to give a short-term boost to the currency and the government as it prepares to present its austere 1997 budget to parliament.
But the good news was tempered by an unemployment rate stuck at a record 12.5 percent and by signs that the downward move in the number of jobless was probably an aberration.

Economists said they did not expect the upward trend in unemployment to stop in the months ahead. They pointed to the International Labour Organisation unemployment data which showed a 14,000 rise in the number of unemployed.
The sharp reaction by U.S. markets took the wind out of French markets late in the session but could not undo all the territory gained.
Economists said French markets would probably continue to do well until more economic data showed that the unemployment report was just a blip.
Next week, debt markets in France and around the world will be looking forward to the July U.S. unemployment report.
U.S. analysts expect non-farm payrolls to have expanded by 238,000 in July, giving an unemployment rate of 5.3 percent.
